open_obligations: Check the authors' own limitation that inserted bugs differ in distribution from natural LLM errors.
Note the domain change from summarisation to code, where bugs are more objectively checkable.
Check whether reference bugs reduce over-trust in critiques or only make critique-bug inclusion measurable.
out.other_title: No ground truth for topic-based summarization; labelers may over-trust model critiques
out.rationale: Saunders et al. state their summarisation task has no objective way to validate answers or critiques and that labelers may over-trust critiques. McAleese et al. have contractors insert subtle bugs into model-written code, verified to be missed by a critic at least once, and use these tamper descriptions as reference bugs for rating critiques; they also report critics trained without tampering severely underperform, but inserted bugs differ from natural errors.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how to obtain reference flaws for evaluating critiques when the base task lacks objective ground truth, for LLM critiques of code

text: The paper collects training data by having contractors insert subtle bugs into model-written code, verifying with access to an LLM critic that it misses each bug in at least one of three samples (not strictly enforced). The authors report this adversarial collection noticeably increased bug subtlety, and the critic used was updated twice, so much data was adversarial to ChatGPT and much to an early CriticGPT.
title: Adversarial tampering: humans insert subtle bugs that an LLM critic misses
